theory.intro: PAYG instalments only estimate the tax owed. At the end of the financial year a tax return compares the **total instalments** withheld with the **total tax payable**. Too much withheld gives a **tax refund**; too little leaves a **tax liability** owing to the ATO.
facts: $\text{Refund or amount owing}=\text{Total instalments}-\text{Total tax payable}$
A positive result is a refund; a negative result is an amount owing, equal in size to that negative number.
When the two totals are equal there is neither a refund nor an amount owing.
$\text{Total tax payable}=\text{Income tax payable}+\text{Medicare levy}$, so include the levy before comparing.
$\text{Total instalments}=\text{Instalment per pay period}\times\text{Number of pay periods}$, using $52$ weeks, $26$ fortnights or $12$ months in a year.
steps: Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments

workedExamples.question_text:
For each worker, determine whether there is a tax refund or an amount owing, and state the amount.
(a) Amelia paid $\$8400$ in PAYG instalments and has total tax payable of $\$7650$.
(b) Ben paid $\$6200$ in PAYG instalments and has total tax payable of $\$6980$.
(c) Chen paid $\$5100$ in PAYG instalments and has total tax payable of $\$5100$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=8400-7650\\&=\$750\end{aligned}$
The instalments exceed the tax payable, so Amelia receives a refund of $\$750.00$.

(b)
$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=6200-6980\\&=-\$780\end{aligned}$
The instalments are less than the tax payable, so Ben owes $\$780.00$.

(c)
$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=5100-5100\\&=\$0\end{aligned}$
The totals are equal, so Chen has neither a refund nor an amount owing.

workedExamples.question_text:
Priya worked for $32$ weeks and had $\$215.50$ withheld from each weekly pay. Her total tax payable for the year is $\$6540$.
Determine her tax refund or amount owing.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total instalments}&=215.50\times32\\&=\$6896\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=6896-6540\\&=\$356\end{aligned}$
Priya paid more than the tax payable, so she receives a refund of $\$356.00$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Marcus has income tax payable of $\$12\,480.60$ and a Medicare levy of $\$1460$. He had $\$520$ withheld from each of his $26$ fortnightly pays.
Determine his tax refund or amount owing.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total tax payable}&=12\,480.60+1460\\&=\$13\,940.60\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Total instalments}&=520\times26\\&=\$13\,520\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=13\,520-13\,940.60\\&=-\$420.60\end{aligned}$
Marcus has not paid enough tax, so he owes $\$420.60$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Elena's total annual tax payable is $\$14\,456$. She receives $26$ fortnightly pays.
What equal fortnightly PAYG instalment would leave her with neither a refund nor an amount owing?
workedExamples.solution_text:
For neither a refund nor an amount owing, total instalments must equal total tax payable.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Fortnightly instalment}&=14\,456\div26\\&=\$556.00\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Noah has an annual taxable income of $\$58\,600$. He had $\$350$ withheld from each of his $26$ fortnightly pays.
For taxable incomes from $\$45\,001$ to $\$120\,000$, the supplied tax table gives income tax of $\$5092$ plus $32.5$ cents for each dollar over $\$45\,000$.
Use this table rule to determine his tax refund or amount owing. Ignore the Medicare levy.
workedExamples.solution_text:
His taxable income falls in the supplied bracket.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Excess}&=58\,600-45\,000\\&=\$13\,600\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Tax payable}&=5092+0.325\times13\,600\\&=5092+4420\\&=\$9512\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Total instalments}&=350\times26\\&=\$9100\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=9100-9512\\&=-\$412\end{aligned}$
Noah has not paid enough tax, so he owes $\$412.00$.

foundation.question_text:
A seasonal grape picker has a tax payable of $\$5318$ and his PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$4975$.
Does he receive a tax refund or does he have an amount owing?
Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
Compare the two totals.
$4975<5318$
The instalments withheld are less than the tax payable, so he has not paid enough tax and has an amount owing.

foundation.question_text:

foundation.solution_text:
1. **Find the total instalments paid**
$\text{Total instalments}=318.50\times52$
$=\$16\,562$
2. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$16\,562-15\,940=622$
The balance is positive, so he receives a tax refund of $\$622.00$.

mastery.question_text:
A parcel courier has a taxable income of $\$67\,400$ and had PAYG instalments of $\$425$ withheld each fortnight for $26$ fortnights.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to determine his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent.
Ignore the Medicare levy.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the total tax payable**
$\text{Total tax payable}=5092+0.325\times(67\,400-45\,000)$
$=5092+0.325\times22\,400$
$=\$12\,372$
2. **Find the total instalments paid**
$\text{Total instalments}=425\times26$
$=\$11\,050$
3. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$11\,050-12\,372=-1322$
The balance is negative, so he has an amount owing of $\$1322.00$.

mastery.question_text:
Two couriers each have a tax payable of $\$14\,872$.
Anh had $\$560$ withheld each fortnight for $26$ fortnights, while Bede had $\$1290$ withheld each month for $12$ months.
Determine each courier’s tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Anh's instalments}=560\times26$
$=\$14\,560$
$14\,560-14\,872=-312$
Anh has an amount owing of $\$312.00$.
$\text{Bede's instalments}=1290\times12$
$=\$15\,480$
$15\,480-14\,872=608$
Bede receives a tax refund of $\$608.00$.
